threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie when they still flinch at the sound of a busker outside the station, expecting a quiet commute.
Caught a night bus last week and a guy was handing out fruit. Turns out it was all from his mum’s garden. Brixton’s quirks never cease to amaze.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The first time I spotted a cat lounging on a balcony, sunbathing as if it owned the place, I thought, 'Yep, I'm home now.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden café serving €1.50 coffee, nestled between two graffiti-covered walls, with a cat that rules the place.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their tiptoeing past the Mission’s cloudy afternoons. Outsiders just pull on a sweater—they don't know it’ll burn off by noon.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit hold the Muni doors open for an elderly woman while she balanced a massive bouquet. Just a moment, but it felt so San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and parks, but it’s the hidden taverna on Carrer de Perill where the real local vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at crossing the street during the 'green man' phase. It's like they're waiting for a signal from the universe.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'TfL'—everyone here knows it's just part of the transport family.
Caught a night bus home and saw a chap in a full tuxedo arguing with a traffic cone, like it was his long-lost friend. London, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a kid selling homemade lemonade next to a pile of abandoned bicycles, I knew this place had its own pulse.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You'd think buskers in the U-Bahn are all about music, but there's a guy in Kreuzberg juggling flaming torches while balancing on a unicycle. A whole performance!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here when they get off BART at 16th and don’t flinch at the smell of street tacos mixed with the faint whiff of recent street cleaning.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy playing the accordion on the 6 tonight. The bus was packed, but his tune made everyone smile—even the guy in a suit who usually stares at his phone.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for pictures, but locals use them for proper conversations over coffee, day or night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look up at the buildings; locals have perfected the art of walking while staring at their phones.
